shapes/fwd: Take a node that computes z equals W times x. Here W has two rows and three columns, x has three entries, and z has two.
shapes/dz: Backprop hands this node the gradient on z: one number per entry of z, so two of them. Call it d z.
shapes/dwshape: The gradient on W must have the shape of W, two by three: one number for every entry of W.
shapes/outer: From a column of two and a row of three, only one product makes a two by three grid: the outer product, d z times x transpose.
shapes/dxshape: The gradient on x must have the shape of x: three numbers. W transpose is three by two, and times d z it gives exactly three.
entries/zi: Why the outer product? Each entry z i adds up W i j times x j over j. So nudging W i j moves z i by x j times the nudge.
entries/ij: Its gradient is d z i times x j: the gradient on its row's entry of z, times its column's entry of x. Row one, column two: minus two times two, minus four.
entries/grid: Fill the grid. In row zero, d z is one, so the row is x itself: three, zero, and two. In row one it is minus two: minus six, zero, and minus four.
entries/dx: And each x j feeds every entry of z, so its gradients add up over the rows: column j of W, weighted by d z. For x zero, one times one plus minus one times minus two: three.
